answer: Inter-arrival spacing floor enforces a minimum delay between an agent's first and subsequent actions, checked against a rolling median. Honest agents wander across variable timing, but a farm must stagger thousands of identities, pushing each toward the nadir of throughput. Sybils that burst in lockstep get throttled to the slowest allowed cadence, so the attacker's real cost is wall-clock time per identity plus idle capacity held open. Each fake agent must anchor its schedule to survive the spacing check, multiplying attacker overhead by the number of identities kept alive.
